If response.body is null or undefined, the function returns true without writing the file, which is misleading. The caller expects the file to exist when true is returned. Consider returning false or throwing an error when response.body is missing, as this indicates a download failure.
```suggestion
        if (!response.body) {
          log.error("failed to download", { url, reason: "missing response body" })
          return false
        }
        await Filesystem.writeStream(dest, response.body)
```

`ToolContext` adds a new required `lsp` field. Since `@opencode-ai/plugin` is a public package, making this non-optional is a breaking type change for any external host that constructs a `ToolContext`. Consider making it optional (`lsp?: LspContext`) or ensure a major version bump/release note accompanies this change.
```suggestion
  lsp?: LspContext
```

The casts here (`as Promise<Record<string, LspDiagnostic[]>>` and `diagnostic as any`) unnecessarily discard type safety. `LSP.diagnostics()` already returns diagnostics structurally compatible with `LspDiagnostic`, and `LspDiagnostic` is structurally compatible with `LSPClient.Diagnostic` used by `LSP.Diagnostic.pretty`. Prefer removing the casts (or narrowing to `unknown` if needed) so mismatches are caught by the compiler.
```suggestion
              diagnostics: () => LSP.diagnostics(),
              diagnosticPretty: (diagnostic: LspDiagnostic) =>
                LSP.Diagnostic.pretty(diagnostic),
```

There’s existing test coverage for `ToolRegistry` (e.g. `packages/opencode/test/tool/registry.test.ts`), but this new `ctx.lsp` surface isn’t validated. Add/extend a registry test that loads a custom tool and asserts `ctx.lsp` exists (and optionally that its functions are callable/mocked) to prevent regressions in the plugin context wiring.

`hover` is declared as returning `Promise<any>`, but the underlying `LSP.hover` implementation returns an array of results (one per active LSP client) and may include `null` entries. To avoid surprising plugin authors and improve type safety, update the return type/documentation to reflect an array (e.g. `Promise<unknown[]>` or `Promise<(unknown|null)[]>`) and consider filtering/normalizing results in the wrapper.
```suggestion
  /** Get hover information at a position (one result per active LSP client; entries may be null). */
  hover(input: { file: string; line: number; character: number }): Promise<(unknown | null)[]>
```

This interceptor reads beta flags from the SDK/provider *settings* (`options["betas"]` / `options["headers"]["anthropic-beta"]`), but betas set via the `chat.params` hook are passed at call-time through `providerOptions` and typically end up in the actual request init (e.g. `opts.headers`). As a result, plugin-supplied betas still won’t be injected into the Vertex request body. Consider deriving the beta set from the per-request init (normalize `opts.headers` whether it’s a `Headers`, array tuples, or object) and merging with any provider-config defaults.

The current logic only injects `anthropic_beta` when the body doesn’t already contain it. If the underlying SDK (or a future change) starts sending `anthropic_beta` (or an empty array) and the user also configures betas via headers/`options.betas`, the configured betas won’t be merged/deduplicated. Consider always normalizing/merging into `body.anthropic_beta` (treating an existing string/array value as input) and deduplicating before re-serializing.

This test re-implements the production dedup logic with a local `Set`, so it can pass even if the fetch interceptor stops injecting/deduplicating betas. It would be more robust to assert on the actual outgoing request body by mocking the Vertex Anthropic provider’s `fetch` (or extracting the injection into a helper that can be unit-tested) and verifying `anthropic_beta` is set and deduplicated.

`@aws-sdk/credential-providers` and `google-auth-library` are now imported at module load time, but they’re only needed for the Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex code paths. This makes startup/compile heavier and forces these Node-oriented deps to be resolved even when those providers aren’t used. Consider switching back to lazy `import()` inside the relevant loaders (without `BunProc.install`, since the deps are now in package.json) so they’re only loaded when required.

`expand()` handles `~/...` but not the Windows-style `~\...` form, even though other parts of this change (e.g. `Session.addWorkspaceDirectory` and `directoryPath`) explicitly support `~\\`. This will make `/add-directory ~\...` directory suggestions behave incorrectly on Windows. Consider updating `expand()` (and any other path expansion helpers here) to also expand `~\\` when `HOME` is set.
```suggestion
  const home = process.env.HOME
  if (input === "~") return home ?? input
  if (home && (input.startsWith("~/") || input.startsWith("~\\"))) {
```

`File.search()` now calls `external(sessionID)` on every invocation. That helper does a DB lookup (`Session.get`) and then walks each allowed external directory via `Ripgrep.files`, which can be very expensive during autocomplete (many calls per keystroke) and may cause noticeable latency on large directories. Consider caching external directory file/dir lists per session (keyed by permission set + maybe a short TTL), or precomputing them when a workspace directory is added, so search remains fast.

`toolbeam-docs-theme@0.4.8` declares peer dependencies `astro: ^5.7.13` and `@astrojs/starlight: ^0.34.3` (see bun.lock). With `astro` now set to 5.17.3 (and Starlight bumped), this will be an unsatisfied peer range and may break the docs theme integration. Consider upgrading `toolbeam-docs-theme` to a version compatible with Astro 5.17.x / Starlight 0.37.x, or keep Astro/Starlight pinned to versions that satisfy the theme’s peer requirements.

The checkout function doesn't verify if the target branch is already checked out in another worktree before attempting to switch. While the UI prevents this scenario, direct API calls could still attempt to checkout a branch that's in use elsewhere. Consider adding a worktree check before the checkout operation to provide a clear error message instead of relying on git's error output. This would make the API behavior more predictable and provide better error messages to API consumers.

The worktree parsing logic only captures worktrees with branches (line 169-170) but ignores worktrees in detached HEAD state. When a worktree is in detached HEAD state, the porcelain output includes a "HEAD" line with the commit hash instead of a "branch" line. This means detached HEAD worktrees won't be tracked in the `occupied` map, potentially allowing users to switch to the same commit from multiple worktrees. Consider adding handling for the "HEAD" line to track detached HEAD worktrees or document this limitation.

When a user selects a remote branch from the UI (e.g., "origin/feature"), the checkout logic first checks if a local branch with the extracted name exists (e.g., "feature") and switches to it if found. This means selecting "origin/feature" could switch to a local "feature" branch that may have diverged from the remote, rather than fetching and tracking the remote branch. Consider checking if the local branch is tracking the intended remote before switching, or provide feedback to the user when this situation occurs. The current behavior matches standard git behavior but might be unexpected in a UI context where the user explicitly selected a remote branch.

On session switch, `store.mode` is not reset/restored. If the user is in `shell` mode in one session and switches sessions, the new session can inherit `shell` mode and submit the restored/empty input via `sdk.client.session.shell(...)` unexpectedly. Consider resetting mode to `normal` when changing sessions (or persisting/restoring mode per session along with the draft).
```suggestion

        // Reset mode on session change to avoid inheriting modes like "shell"
        setStore("mode", "normal")
```

With `drafts` now imported/used here, session deletion in this dialog (the delete keybind handler below) should also clear any saved draft for the deleted session. Otherwise drafts for deleted sessions can accumulate and potentially be restored later if the ID is referenced again.

`timeoutMs` is read from `(config.experimental as any)?.task_timeout_ms`, but `Config.Info`'s `experimental` schema does not include `task_timeout_ms` (and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default). As a result, this setting can’t actually be configured via opencode.json[c] as described. Add `task_timeout_ms` to the config schema (ideally as a positive int) and then read it without `any` casts.
```suggestion
      const experimentalTimeout =
        (config.experimental as { task_timeout_ms?: unknown } | undefined)?.task_timeout_ms
      const timeoutMs =
        typeof experimentalTimeout === "number" &&
        Number.isFinite(experimentalTimeout) &&
        experimentalTimeout > 0
          ? Math.floor(experimentalTimeout)
          : DEFAULT_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS
```

`setTimeout` effectively caps delays at a 32-bit signed int; if `timeoutMs` is configured above ~2,147,483,647 or is non-finite/NaN, Node/Bun will clamp/convert it and the timer may fire immediately. Validate/coerce `timeoutMs` (finite number, >0) and clamp to the max supported delay before passing it to `setTimeout`.

The completion log uses `(result.info as any).finish`, which defeats the type-safety you get from `MessageV2.Info`. Consider narrowing (`if (result.info.role === "assistant")`) and then logging `result.info.finish` (or logging `undefined` when it’s not an assistant) instead of using `any`.
```suggestion
        finish: result.info.role === "assistant" ? result.info.finish : undefined,
```

`Agent.get(lastUser.agent)` is now executed before checking for pending `subtask`/`compaction` work. In iterations where `task?.type` is `subtask` or `compaction`, this fetch is unused because the loop `continue`s before normal processing. Moving the agent lookup down into the normal-processing branch avoids an extra async read on those iterations.
```suggestion

```

After `if (item.info.role === "user") continue`, `item.info` should be narrowed to `MessageV2.Assistant`, so `(item.info as any).finish` should be replaceable with `item.info.finish`. Avoiding `any` here prevents silently logging incorrect fields if the message union changes.
```suggestion
      log.info("loop: returning result", { sessionID, finish: item.info.finish, textLen })
```

Good catch — you're right that plugin-supplied betas via `chat.params` flow through `providerOptions` in `streamText` rather than into the `options` object the interceptor reads here. That's a real gap for the general case.

For this PR's immediate use case, the 1M shadow model entries bake `anthropic-beta` into `model.headers`, which gets merged into `options["headers"]` in `getSDK()` before the SDK is constructed, so the interceptor does catch it. But a plugin that sets `output.options.betas` via `chat.params` without using a shadow model would not be covered.

Fixing the general case (deriving betas from per-request `opts.headers`) would be a good follow-up, but adds complexity around normalizing the `Headers` object vs plain object vs array-of-tuples forms. Happy to take that on in a separate PR if that's preferred.

Valid — the `if (!body.anthropic_beta)` guard means if the SDK ever starts pre-populating `anthropic_beta` (e.g. as an empty array), configured betas would be silently dropped. Agreed this should always merge and deduplicate. Will update to normalize and spread into a `Set` regardless of whether the key already exists.

Agreed, it's tautological. The test was a placeholder while we validated the approach, but it doesn't actually exercise the interceptor. Will remove it — the config-parsing tests (headers and betas array) are the ones with real value here.

This test re-implements the shadow-variant behavior with local data instead of asserting on production state, so it can pass even if the actual variant registration in `provider.ts` changes or breaks. Replace it with assertions against `Provider.list()`/`Provider.getModel()` for `google-vertex-anthropic` (e.g., `*-1m` models exist, `api.id` points to the source model, `limit.context` is 1_000_000, and the beta flag is present).

There’s no test that exercises the new Vertex request-body injection (`anthropic_beta`) end-to-end. Add a test that mocks `globalThis.fetch` (or the provider `fetch` option) to capture `init.body` for a `google-vertex-anthropic` POST and assert the outgoing JSON contains `anthropic_beta` with deduped values sourced from config headers and/or `options.betas`.

The fetch interceptor reads betas from the SDK construction-time `options` (provider config + `model.headers`). Betas set at call-time via the `chat.params` hook end up in `params.options` → `providerOptions` passed to `streamText`, and do not affect `provider.options` used here, so plugins setting `output.options.betas` still won’t be forwarded for Vertex requests unless they also modify config/model headers. Either update the PR description to reflect this limitation, or change the interceptor to derive betas from the per-request init (e.g., normalize/read `opts.headers` and/or other per-request fields) so `chat.params`-supplied betas are actually injected.

`new Set<string>(options["betas"] ?? [])` will behave incorrectly if `options.betas` is configured as a string (it will iterate characters) or other non-array iterable. Consider normalizing to a string[] (e.g., accept array, accept comma-separated string, otherwise ignore) and filtering out empty/whitespace-only entries before merging.

This code assumes `opts.body` is a JSON string; `JSON.parse(opts.body as string)` will throw (and break the request) if the SDK provides a non-string body or already-serialized non-JSON payload. Add a guard like `typeof opts.body === "string"` and handle parse failures gracefully (skip injection) so the interceptor can’t take down requests unexpectedly.

The TUI process can't use `Bus.publish` for renderer suspend/resume acks: `Bus` is instance-scoped (requires `Instance.directory` context) and is not shared with the backend Worker, so this will either throw or never reach `TerminalControl`'s `Bus.subscribe` listeners. Send the ack back to the backend via the SDK (e.g., `sdk.client.tui.publish(...)` to `/tui/publish`) so the ack is published on the backend bus for the correct instance/directory.

Same issue as above for the resume path: publishing the resume ack via `Bus.publish` from the TUI process won't reach the backend (and may throw due to missing `Instance` context). Use the SDK `tui.publish` API (or another backend RPC) to publish the ack on the backend bus so `TerminalControl` can observe it.

`subscriptionsInitialized` is module-global, but `Bus.subscribe(...)` registers handlers in an instance-scoped subscription map (keyed by `Instance.directory`). After the first instance initializes this, subsequent instances will skip subscribing and `TerminalControl` will never receive ack events (it will always time out). Track subscription initialization per instance (e.g., via `Instance.state(...)` or a `Map<directory, boolean>`), not a single global boolean.
What is `GlobalInfo` for? I don't see it used anywhere
Still valid — this is the same feedback from the first review. Will remove it; the config-parsing tests cover the meaningful surface area.

Agreed it would be more robust. The challenge is the test infra required to intercept the fetch call inside the SDK — it would need to mock globalThis.fetch before SDK construction and verify the body after the interceptor runs. Worth doing but it's enough test infrastructure work that I'd rather leave it as a follow-up than block this PR on it. The interceptor itself is straightforward to audit manually.

Correct — updating the PR description to reflect this limitation explicitly. The interceptor intentionally only covers betas sourced from provider config and model.headers (which is how the 1M shadow models work). Plugin-supplied betas via chat.params are a separate gap to address in a follow-up.
Good catch. Will normalize: if betas is a string, split on comma; if array, use as-is; otherwise ignore. Will also filter empty/whitespace entries.
Valid — will add a `typeof opts.body === "string"` guard and wrap the parse in try/catch to skip injection on failure rather than throwing.

Using `Config.Keybinds` (with per-field defaults) inside the per-file `tui.json` schema means any file that sets *one* keybind will parse into a fully-populated object and then `mergeDeep` will overwrite keybind customizations from lower-precedence configs back to defaults. To preserve the documented deep-merge behavior, consider parsing `keybinds` as an overrides-only record/partial object, merge those, then apply `Config.Keybinds.parse(...)` once on the final merged result to fill defaults.
```suggestion
    // Parse keybind overrides only; defaults will be applied later using Config.Keybinds
    keybinds: z.record(z.unknown()).optional(),
```

TUI migration parses `opencode.json{,c}` via `parseJsonc(source)` without collecting/handling parse errors. For invalid JSONC, this may silently produce a partial object and trigger migration/stripping unexpectedly. Consider parsing with an `errors` array (and skipping migration when errors are present), or reusing `ConfigPaths.parseText(...)` so migration only runs on syntactically valid configs.

`ConfigPaths` now centralizes config file reading/parsing logic, but `Config.load()` still maintains its own env/file substitution + JSONC parsing implementation. This duplication makes it easy for server config and TUI config to diverge in behavior (e.g., comment-handling, missing-token behavior, error formatting). Consider switching `Config.load()` to reuse `ConfigPaths.parseText(...)` (or extracting a shared helper) so both config systems stay consistent.

Docs say `scroll_speed` has minimum `1`, but the TUI schema allows values down to `0.001` (and tests use a non-integer). Either update the docs to match the schema/behavior (including that decimals are allowed), or tighten the schema if `1` is the intended minimum.
```suggestion
- `scroll_speed` - Controls how fast the TUI scrolls when using scroll commands (minimum: `0.001`, supports decimal values). Defaults to `3`. **Note: This is ignored if `scroll_acceleration.enabled` is set to `true`.**
```

This tip suggests enabling `scroll_acceleration`, but the config shape is an object that requires `scroll_acceleration.enabled: true`. As written, users may try `"scroll_acceleration": true`, which will be rejected by the schema / ignored. Suggest rewording to explicitly mention `scroll_acceleration.enabled`.
```suggestion
  "Enable {highlight}scroll_acceleration.enabled{/highlight} in {highlight}tui.json{/highlight} for smooth macOS-style scrolling",
```

Test name says `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG` takes precedence over project config, but the assertions (and inline comment) verify the opposite (project config wins). Rename the test to reflect the actual precedence being enforced to avoid future confusion/regressions.
```suggestion
test("project config takes precedence over OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG", async () => {
```
We should avoid using 'any' for typing. See [Contributing guidelines](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#style-preferences)

For `google-vertex-anthropic`, Vertex rejects the `anthropic-beta` *HTTP header* (it must be sent as the `anthropic_beta` JSON body field). This interceptor injects `anthropic_beta` but it does not remove `anthropic-beta` from the outgoing request headers, so requests will still fail when the beta is configured via `options.headers` or via the new 1M model variants’ `model.headers`. After extracting the header value, strip `anthropic-beta` from `opts.headers` (handle object/Headers/tuple-array forms) and/or avoid passing it to the SDK as a header for this provider.

When normalizing beta flags, values taken from `options.betas` (array form) and from an existing `body.anthropic_beta` are only *filtered* with `trim()` but then added to the `Set` without trimming. This can preserve leading/trailing whitespace and defeat deduplication (and potentially send invalid beta names). Consider adding trimmed values (`betaSet.add(b.trim())`) for both sources and filtering non-string entries defensively.

The new in-memory registration of the `*-1m` Vertex Anthropic model variants isn’t covered by a test. Since this logic directly affects the model picker/UI (model presence, `api.id` remap, and `limit.context`), consider adding a lightweight assertion in the provider tests that `Provider.list()` includes these `*-1m` models (when the source models exist) and that they have the expected `limit.context`, `api.id`, and beta flag metadata.
Good catch — this is a real bug. Fixed: now strips `anthropic-beta` from `opts.headers` after collecting the value, handling all three header forms (`Headers` object, plain object, array-of-tuples).
Fixed — now trims before adding to the Set for all sources (betas array, existing body values). Also added `.map(b => b.trim())` in the array normalization path.

Fair point on coverage. We've verified the variants are registered correctly via the live server API (confirmed `claude-sonnet-4-6-1m@default` and `claude-sonnet-4-5-1m@20250929` present with `limit.context: 1_000_000`), but adding it to the test suite would make it reproducible. Will add an integration test against `Provider.list()` for the 1M variants.

With `include` undefined, `nodir` becomes false and directories will be included by default. ```

The `bun add` install step still ignores the exit code (you `await ...exited` but don’t check the result). If `bun add` fails (network, permissions, registry issues), this will continue and attempt to run the server anyway, leading to a later/less clear failure. Capture the exit code and either log a useful error and return, or throw so the caller marks the server as broken.

The `bun add pyright` installer awaits `.exited` but ignores the exit code. If installation fails, this will proceed to run the langserver path that may not exist, making failures harder to diagnose. Please check the exit code and handle non-zero (log + return/throw).

This install step awaits `.exited` but does not check the exit code. A failed `bun add svelte-language-server` will still proceed and likely fail later when spawning the server. Check the exit code and handle failures explicitly (log and return/throw).
